utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll go into closed session for the witness to be brought in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, sir. Your evidence will now continue. Please remember that the solemn declaration you took at the beginning to tell the truth continues to apply to your evidence throughout. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you move on, first of all, has that got a number?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. This is (redacted) number P2376.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And you maintain that you did not know or notice anything at that time about this killing of a hundred -- more than a hundred men in a barn in the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you saw only one or two houses burning in the area while you were there. Where were those houses, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: From where you were positioned, could you actually see the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: So you're saying you could have seen it if houses in the centre of the village had been burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could have seen it, but I can't remember at this very moment where it is relative to the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you left this headquarter established at the main road, around which date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall now which date it was, whether it was the 27th, 28th, 29th. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And where did your unit go from there? What was your next deployment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, our company left towards Orahovac, and the next operation for us was Milanovici and Malishevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you see -- did you see any other units in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Frenki's men for about 10 minutes and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And the area where you saw Frenki's men, did you depict that on the map that we had a look at yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we do not need to call it up again unless you like to have a look at it again. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you -- are you finished with the fallout from the video clip?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is your suggestion that this witness knows more than he's prepared to say? If that's what you're trying to do, have a go at him and find out, but don't play us video clips that make suggestions and then ask a few mild-mannered questions that don't -- if this man's position has to be tested, then it's your duty to test it. I'm left wondering what's the purpose unless you're actually going to ask some challenging questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, maybe you don't have a basis for it, in which case I then wonder why -- what we're doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Well -- yes. I would -- can I -- with Your Honour's leave, can I finish the other deployments of the witness and then get back at that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: The next deployment after the one towards Orahovac, according to your statement, was liberating the Pec-Kula-Rozaje road, and in the statement it says it was in early April, 1999. This is page 6 of the statement, Your Honours. Did you see other units involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And the deployment after that you describe in your statement as having been around the Radonjic Lake, Supod, Lapodnica. Were there any VJ, MUP or JSO units involved in this operation to your knowledge? Did you see any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, here in the transcript it says something else. That's not what I heard in the interpretation, whether MUP units were involved, yes. What is this about JSO? In any case, that's not the interpretation that I got.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I asked you whether in this operation any units of the MUP or the JSO or the VJ were involved and whether you saw those, any of those.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Only the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And the last deployment you talk about in your statement, late April, early May, was in the Suva Reka area, Budakovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: This is page 6 still of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Were there any VJ units, MUP units or JSO units involved in this operation to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And that was your last deployment. When did you leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. Sometime in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we call up Exhibit P99 again, please. Page two, please. Now, we looked at this exhibit yesterday, and you marked in the upper-left corner the approximate position your unit was, and when I talked about the centre of the village today, I was referring to the part of the village which is in the right-hand side of the photo where a vertical street is going up. I ask you again, could you see from where you were, could you see into this part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: So which part of the village could you see? Because earlier you said yes, you could see the village. Could you mark which parts you could see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And while you were there during the three or four days, you did see two -- one or two houses burning, and you don't recall where? Do you stand by this account?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And this part that you just encircled, you did not see any houses burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really say. I was looking from the other side. I was not looking from this perspective.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And when you left the village, or when you left the location and moved on to your next deployment, how would you describe the -- the state of the village? Was it intact? Was it destroyed? What kind of destruction, if any, did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And the house in the vicinity of the Hajdari compound in which the six prisoners of war were shot, you say in your statement it was burned. When was that house burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact date. Everything happened very quickly, but it happened while we were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Was it close to the killing event or the next day or the second next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the time. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's as far as I think I can take it on this point here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Can we take a snapshot of the picture, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have an objection to this photograph. Your Honour, the reason is very simple. If the Prosecutor wanted to test the witness, then it would have been fair to have shown the photograph from the perspective from which he was looking, and they have the resources to do that. This is an aerial photograph, one. Second, it shows much more than he could have seen from his position. And in fact, I don't see how this photograph can really help us in terms of what the witness could or could not have seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These are all issues of weight of the evidence and they're matters on which you can cross-examine the witness, so we will admit the snapshot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Can we call up Exhibit P2015, please. 2015.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this exhibit that the Prosecution wants to show this witness now is, in our opinion, completely inappropriate for admission through this witness and in general. This witness, as he told us himself, used to be a junior sergeant in the police, and he had no direct impact and no direct knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: First of all, what is this exhibit so that -- can I see the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: The exhibit -- if I may assist, the exhibit is a Joint Command order of the 23rd March, 1999, and we are not intending to tender this document through the witness, but I would like him to comment on the operation that is described therein and whether this relates in any way to the operation that he participated in, in his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the light of that, Mr. Petrovic, do you maintain the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am satisfied with one part of the answer, namely when the Prosecutor says that she did not intend and does not wish to tender this through this witness. That much is okay. But all questions that may be asked of this witness go beyond anything that he could have had direct knowledge about, and all such questions would be inappropriate. So I'm happy with the answer, but I don't think it is -- I think it is pointless to ask questions about this document of this particular witness. Of course, it is up to you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, these are the matters for argument in due course. What the witness is going to be asked about is how what's set out in the order compares with what happened on the ground, and that seems to me a perfectly legitimate exercise, and indeed it may actually go to the question of whether the document on its own might ever stand as a piece of evidence on its own in due course because it could contribute to its -- our assessment of its reliability. However, for present purposes, all that will happen is the part that's referred to will be admitted in the context in which it was used so that we can fully understand the evidence that's given, and we note the objection you take to the exhibit in principle. So carry on, please, Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Indeed I have very specific paragraphs I want to address. It would be page 3, paragraph 5 and 5.1. This is in both the English and the B/C/S version. It's the same page and paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, could you have a look at paragraph 5 and 5.1. Can you read it? To yourself, I mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Would that generally reflect what you understood your unit was taking part in, kind of operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document shows some general operation that was likely, but all I know about is the blockade of the road from Velika Krusa to Mala Krusa, and I have not even heard of half of these places.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we move then to Exhibit 1981, please. It would be page 3, paragraphs 5.4 and 5.5 in the B/C/S version, and it would be page 4 with the same paragraphs in the English version. And the document that is pulled up is an order of the 449th Motorised Brigade, dated 23rd March, 1999. Yes. Can you zoom in paragraphs 5.4 and 5.5, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, could you have a look at these two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen in front of me. I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Do you have it now? Can you see it now? Okay. Could you please look at paragraph 5.4 and 5.5.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I just have it in B/C/S. I don't have it in English. I'd kind of like to see what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have the English version, please. Can you get it, Mr. Ackerman, on your LiveNote screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's here now, Your Honour. I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sir, these two paragraphs, would they reflect generally what you experienced and described in your statement as the operation of which your unit was part of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In paragraph 5.4, I didn't participate in that. That must have been done the day before, since the wine cellar had already been liberated by the time we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And paragraph 5.5, what would you comment on this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We took part in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we go to page 5 in the English version, paragraph 8.2. In B/C/S, it's page 4 of the same document. Can you have a look at 8.2. The first paragraph where it refers to the wine cellars in Mala Krusa. You must mentioned the wine cellars. Were you aware that this was a concentration point for prisoners of war to be brought there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can we now call up Exhibit P1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Moeller, I need just a little bit more time to digest the contents of each one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Certainly. Thank you. Could we call up Exhibit P1995, please. And the first page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: This document is the analysis of an operation carried out, and it's dated 30 March, 1999. Sir, could you have a look at the first paragraph in this document. It talks about an operation in the period between 25 and 29 March, so in the period when you were in the area around Mala Krusa. Could you look at this paragraph and tell us whether that would generally describe the operation you took part in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In principle, it does show that, but I don't know about all the locations mentioned here, and I don't know the exact details of the operation because I was assigned my own separate area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Very well. Could we go to page 3. In the English version page 3, paragraph 6, and in the B/C/S version it is page 2, paragraph 2. Sir, could you have a look at paragraph 2. The sentence starts with "The formations of the VJ," and then further down it refers to MUP forces having been engaged. Could you have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, the English version is not available, so before there's any answers or anything, I'd like to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could we perhaps have the English version brought up at the same time as the B/C/S in future so we're not delayed by this? I take it yours, like mine, Mr. Ackerman, is set up for the English to come on. You have to actually set it. Now mine's just appeared on the screen only now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, mine appeared at the same time as yours did, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, so they're set that way, I think. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you have a chance in the meantime to read the part listing the MUP forces in paragraph two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you see the detachment you were a member of in this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only see the 23rd detachment of the PJP and we were a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Scrolling down a little bit. In the same paragraph it says: "The total strength of the MUP forces in this overall operation was 1.020 men." To the best of your knowledge, would that be a realistic number from what you observed in your area if you can comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And the overall number of all forces involved in this operation is said to be around 2.000 men. What do you say to this number from your experience in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't speak about the others, but this is the correct figure for the PJP. I didn't meet the other ones, including the army, apart from the force that was with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Now, the same page, scrolling down to the bottom. It refers in the last sentence on this page of the English version, it says: "The coordinated action amongst the forces and the coordination with the MUP forces were functioning well." From your perspective, having been a part of the MUP forces, do you share this assessment? Was the coordination between the VJ and the MUP functioning well in this operation, the operation that you participated in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the last document I would like to call up is Exhibit 1989. And page 3, please, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm working under the assumption that this is -- what's listed as Exhibit P1089 in the 65 ter summary for this witness which would be the minutes of a meeting at the MUP leadership in Kosovo as it's listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the number that's been given I think was 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I know. And that's a number that I do not see on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller, which one is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: It is 1989, and we informed the Defence after we filed the notification that we had a -- had the wrong number put on the notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I think I am talking about the minutes of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I do have an objection to this document, Your Honour, based upon the fact that the witness's statement is very clear and the testimony given in the Milosevic case is very clear that he was never present for any briefings apart from the one briefing in front of the PJP commander and, therefore, I don't see how he can be asked to merely speculate about places where he was not at if in fact this is what the Prosecutor intends to do with this document. So I would object again to it being admitted into evidence for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I'm not inviting the witness to speculate about anything. I would just like to ask him whether he got ever to know about such kind of meetings being held, because one of his commanders was participating in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It sounds like speculation to me, Your Honour. You're asking him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No. Asking him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please, I won't have argument directly between counsel across the courtroom. The Court will be addressed and not parties directly. I hope that's clear. Let me hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: One of the persons listed in this document is Borislav Josipovic. Was he the commander of your detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did he or anyone else in your detachment or your immediate unit ever tell you about meetings held between commanders of the PJP, the SAJ, the JSO, the SUP chiefs, and under attendance of Sreten Lukic and Nikola Sainovic as this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: That would complete my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that should allay your concern, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller, can we go back to P99, page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we bring that up on the e-court. Now, Ms. Moeller, in the evidence of either Krasniqi or Ramadani, there was a photograph used to identify the location of the -- a building in which a large number of people were held, I think overnight, until the morning of the 26th. Can you recollect the number of that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I would have to check that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or can you tell me from this one roughly where that building is located?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the -- to the houses in which -- in the compound of which the persons were then assembled and separated out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: These were the three houses in -- in the lower part of the picture. It was in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we're at the bottom of the picture almost as far as we can be from where the HQ for the witness was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you remember where you were on the morning of the 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was at the position I had indicated. Do you want me to show the place again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I know where that is. I don't need to see it again. When were you first aware that there was an allegation that over a hundred males had been killed in a building into which initially certain people shot and which was then set on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned of it for the first time in 1999, by watching the BBC. By that time, everything had been completed. I saw it on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, when in 1999 do you maintain that you first heard of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once the war against NATO was completed. Sometime after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in the location where you were based, how many others were stationed there on the morning of the 26th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Six or seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The order will be General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, Mr. Milutinovic, Mr. Sainovic, and General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, although I do have questions, Mr. Ackerman has asked to precede me in the ordering, which I have agreed to, so I'll be going after Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You were shown a -- a video a little while back of a telephone conversation between you and a woman in Sarajevo, and when asked about it, you said that that was part of the conversation, that it was not complete. The question I have to ask you is the way it was cut or the portion that was excerpted out, do you feel like that was unfair to you in any way in terms of representing the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in what way do you feel like it was unfair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because at the beginning, she asked me -- well, I can describe the whole conversation and all the questions she asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You can go ahead and do that if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Good afternoon, good afternoon. Sir, since you were in the area of Velika and Mala Krusa between the 24th and the 29th of March 1999, where some atrocities took place, what do you have to say about that? And having in mind that your name was mentioned on one of the indictments of The Hague Tribunal." These are the words she uttered that I remember very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm wondering if we should be in private session at this point. I don't know. I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if we should be in private session at this point. And I don't know. I'm -- I'm just wanting to make sure we're protecting the identity of the witness, and maybe the witness could tell us if he's going to tell us some things that might reveal something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller, what do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I don't see at this point any reason, because I don't know where Mr. Ackerman is taking the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we're alert to it now, Mr. Ackerman. I'm sorry I was momentarily distracted there, and carry on, and if the problem appears to you to get any more likely, then let me know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'll ask you to go ahead and tell us the contents of that conversation, and if you feel like it's going to disclose your identity in any way, then please let me know and we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well. Throughout the conversation, she tried to suggest that I killed or we killed, and she tried to link us with the place where the crime had taken place. And she kept saying, "Where you participated." So the whole conversation boiled down to this "we" or "you."

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so that was the part that was left out, is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that part that was left out, she was making specific accusations against you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now that I saw the footage again, and I realise this was edited by a journalist, what I think is that they were trying to provoke me into saying something that would benefit them. That's why they tried to provoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else you want to tell us about that interview that you thought might have been unfair to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In your statement, on page 4 you talk about being promoted to the rank of corporal, and what you say about that was you were promoted. It was for "recognition for being brave, sacrificing myself for my country, and for exceptional achievements during NATO bombing of Kosovo." When you talk about recognition for being brave, could you describe for us what it was that you did that you felt was bravery, that was recognised as bravery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The promotion I received after the war in 1999 pertained to my overall participation in the operations in Kosovo during 1998 and 1999. It wasn't linked to one event specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Were -- were there times during your participation in Kosovo where you were under enemy fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and almost in all operations. Not almost, in all operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I take it it's the case that you didn't expel any Kosovo Albanians from their homes and force them to leave the country, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you would have reported anyone that you saw doing that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You didn't kill any innocent Albanian civilians, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You'd have reported anyone you saw doing that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You didn't kill or mistreat any prisoners, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you would report it if you had discovered that that was happening, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you didn't shoot at any people in any villages who were not shooting at you, and you would have reported anyone you saw doing that, too, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you talk about a deployment at a place call Jablanica, and you describe that deployment as desperate and useless. Would I be correct in assuming that was because your unit was so heavily outnumbered by the KLA forces there you could accomplish nothing at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for desperate, I didn't say desperate. I even said for the record that it was not an appropriate interpretation. But as for their forces at Jablanica, they outnumbered and outgunned us by far when we were doing that operation, and that's why it wasn't successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I want to talk to you very briefly about the, I think, one or two times when you talked about the VJ being involved in cooperating in the deployments that you were involved in. In all cases, the -- the cooperation of the VJ was to provide heavy weaponry, artillery, and tanks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you never saw that heavy weaponry used against civilians in any way, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You never saw that VJ weaponry fired against any targets other than those that were firing at you. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that -- that all the activity you saw on the part of the VJ was honourable and correct activity for an army at war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At Velika and Mala Krusa, although you described it, there were VJ vehicles there, tanks and others, they did not fire those weapons at all at Velika and Mala Krusa, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. In that operation, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What the VJ did there was sit in a very small sector of that road and do nothing, and you didn't even see the soldiers get out of their vehicles, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did see them. We were their support, because they did not have enough infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. You -- you indicated in your statement that this -- this compound where you were located, that you were using that camp compound to shelter your vehicles and protect them from NATO air activity. Do you remember saying that in your testimony in another trial here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What, if anything, was the VJ doing with regard to the -- the equipment they had there to protect it from NATO attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They used camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now, the unit you were in throughout the time that you were part of that unit was engaged only in anti-terrorist actions and not in activity against civilian populations. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There was a -- a moment in -- in the Milosevic trial where you were asked, speaking of refugees that you had observed, you were asked by the Prosecution this question: "Is it right that you and some of your colleagues made provision for some of those people to have water where otherwise they would not have had water?" And you said this: "I don't understand why they wouldn't have had water otherwise. We policemen were there. They were our citizens, and they got water." That's what you said; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you said "they were our citizens" because you viewed them as fellow citizens, didn't you? As victims of the KLA who were your fellow citizens; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that view of yours that you've just expressed was a common view among the people you served with in your unit, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have one more thing to talk to you about just in fairness to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And to do that I'd like to go into private session, Your Honour, for the protection of the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys representing Sreten Lukic in these proceedings, and I have a number of questions to ask you today to try to clarify the testimony that you gave in your statement in the Milosevic proceedings and here over the past two days. Now, first of all, one of the things you mentioned here in the past two days was there were questions posed to you regarding Frenki's men or the JSO. Just so I can be clear, when we're talking about the deployment of your unit to the Mala Krusa area, am I correct that these units, that is to say the JSO, to your knowledge did not participate in this operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in any event, when we're talking about the JSO, that is a unit that falls under the jurisdiction of the state security services. That would be the RDB; is that correct? The RDB.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as -- as part of the RDB, that is in Serbian, the Resor Dzavne Bezbednosti, the JSO and indeed all state security units were separate and apart from the public security division or department of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But still within the MUP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I'd like to clarify some issues with respect to the organisation that you were a member of, the PJP. Now, first of all, sir, from your statement I gather that you became a member of your SUP, your secretariat's PJP detachment after completing the necessary training; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And even after completing your training to become a PJP member, you remained an ordinary traffic policeman in the secretariat or the SUP of the city where you were based; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at all times you and other members of the PJP would perform your regular duties, in your case as a traffic policeman, but would be then called upon to undertake security detail for specific tasks involving greater risk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- so that is to say the PJP is not the same thing as the SAJ. The PJP is not a Special Police Unit whose members are permanently tasked in carrying out special or anti-terrorist activities, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct in stating that the purpose of the PJP, when it is deployed, is to prevent major disruptions of public order and peace and in addition to preventing the infiltration of terrorists, includes such things as attendance at public demonstrations, football matches and rallies and to provide public security, that is to say, regular police work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- now, in relation to your PJP detachment, and if you have knowledge of any other PJP detachments prior to 1999 and -- or let's -- prior to 1999, did you have occasion to be engaged in preserving the public peace and order at other venues, including sports matches or other public gatherings that presented a higher concentration of people in other places within the Republic of Serbia, such as Belgrade, Novi Sad, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So that is to say the PJP was not a type of unit that was specifically organised and only utilised to address the security concerns in Kosovo and Metohija, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you would be called up and deployed as a PJP unit and deployed in such cities as Belgrade, Novi Sad, or some other Serbian city, your armaments would be similar to those you had on the ground in Kosovo. Isn't that also right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And regardless of when you were deployed at sporting events in Belgrade or Novi Sad or in the field in Kosovo and Metohija, at all times the uniforms that you, the members of the PJP wore, regardless of whether they were blue camouflage or green camouflage, these uniforms were clearly and unmistakenly marked as belonging to the police. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these uniforms, including any vests or jackets, could be clearly identified from a distance by anyone viewing them because they were clearly identified as the police; is that correct? Based upon the insignia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as a member of the Serbian MUP and also as a PJP member in Kosovo and Metohija, you and your units never cooperated or engaged in any joint actions with any paramilitary formations, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, am I correct that the Serbian police had standing orders to arrest and disarm and detain any and all paramilitaries that were encountered on the terrain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, also, when you were -- when you became a member of the PJP unit, am I correct that your rank within the police force, within the PJP, was identical to the rank which you had had at that same time as a regular traffic policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and these ranks that we talk about, actually, the ranks that are similar to military ranks, that is sergeant, lieutenant, colonel, et cetera, these ranks were not -- did not have the same meaning within the hierarchy of the police as they did in the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, is it accurate that -- that SUP commanders, nacelnici of the SUP, were equal to one another even though they may have different ranks from one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I've understood the previous answer as being that the ranks were the same as military ranks in spite of your interpretation of it, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll clarify then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you clarify for us -- when you said as far as I know, yes, were you trying to say the ranks were the same, had the same function as in the military, or as far as you know they did not have the same function as in the military?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question was the same meaning, not the same function.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Meaning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not have the same meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, it's my misunderstanding then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's okay, Your Honour. I'm glad to have been able to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the -- with respect to the MUP, am I correct that the chains of information and chains of command followed through specific units and structures? Let me know if you can answer that, if you can understand it. Otherwise, I'll break it down to some specifics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. When we talk about the operation of your PJP unit, would it be accurate to state that the lines of command and of informing flowed through the PJP, that is to say you reported to PJP commanders rather than to SUP commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we're at around the time of the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I have just one question before we do break. You were asked about standing orders to arrest, disarm, and detain all paramilitaries encountered on the terrain. Did you ever arrest a paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because we did run into them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you ever see anyone else arresting a paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never in my life have I seen paramilitary formations in our territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The transcript says no because we did run into them. He in fact said we did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And just one final question on the same subject although it might sound slightly repetitive. Have you ever heard of a police officer arresting a paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, we have to break for 20 minutes at this stage. Please stay where you are until we leave the court and then you'll be shown where to wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will go into closed session for the witness to be brought in.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. K25, before the break we had discussed the uniforms worn by the PJP, and I would like to ask you also about the uniforms worn by other units of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. With respect to the uniforms worn by regular policemen and by reserve policemen, am I also correct that those uniforms as well are clearly and conspicuously marked with emblems and insignia so as to be readily identified as being the police of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can now talk about one of the items you discuss in your statement. It starts -- it's discussed at page 20 and at page 22, and that's your identification of Sreten Lukic as the commander of all MUP units in Kosovo. Am I correct that you never actually were present in the Pristina MUP staff and therefore have no actual first-hand knowledge of how that staff operated and what its role was, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that you never met Sreten Lukic while he was in Kosovo at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have knowledge of the fact that there were several other persons in Kosovo at the MUP staff, including Generals Djordjevic and Stevanovic, both of whom were assistant ministers to the minister of the interior Stojiljkovic? They were also in Pristina at various times.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as far as your assertion as to what the MUP staff or the MUP HQ --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you move on, is that question meant to be based on what was thought to be publicly proclaimed the structure, or is it based on actual presence within Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you asking about the question or the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, your previous questions were aimed at establishing that the witness had no personal experience of Mr. Lukic ever being in Kosovo. Now, I'll clarify the position myself. But K25, can you tell me, did you meet any of these persons that were just named in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. That answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, the -- the assertions in your statement where you talk about the operations of the MUP HQ, as you call it, and of Sreten Lukic, am I correct that you have no first-hand knowledge of any of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, as far as all regular and reserve police units in a given municipality are concerned, am I correct that they fall under the jurisdiction and authority of the local municipal secretariat or SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is this true upon the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia, including outside of the province of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that in Kosovo, in Pristina at the time of 1998 and 1999, there was a Pristina secretariat or SUP that was also in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the PJP again, am I correct there was no significant difference between the normal police salary and that of a policeman who also was a member of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some difference, but it was very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I need to go into private session. I have about five or six questions relating to his specific PJP unit, and I would not like to disclose his identity to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall go into private session to -- in the interests of the security of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the time period that you were deployed in Kosovo and Metohija as part of your PJP unit on several occasions in 1998 and 1999, am I correct to say that during those deployments you had the role of an ordinary policeman, that is to say, you yourself were not in any command or staresina position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in your first deployment that you state in your statement, in March of 1998, am I correct that at that time the task of your PJP unit was to secure the road between Klina and Srbica due to the fact that armed terrorists had cut off that road and were conducting armed attacks upon any traffic, civilian or otherwise, travelling on that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- now, you have mentioned that during that portion of your tasking, in that deployment, you were involved in setting up and manning checkpoints on the roadway. Now, if I can ask you, sir, am I correct that these checkpoints were tasked with the objective of inspection of people and vehicles to uncover any weapons, drugs, stolen goods, unlicensed vehicles, persons with outstanding arrest warrants, crime suspects, et cetera? Is that an accurate depiction of the duties that were undertaken at these police checkpoints that were established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we're talking about such police checkpoints, is it a fact that they were used -- that we were not only used exclusively in Kosovo and Metohija at the time, was it the regular practice of the traffic police in the course of their normal duties to utilise such checkpoints for the same reasons and in the same fashion all across Serbia, and for example, in your home city where your SUP is located and where you were a traffic policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it a fact that such traffic checkpoints are still in use throughout Serbia even to this very day on a daily basis by the traffic police of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, later in 1998, your unit was again deployed in Kosovo to secure and liberate the Pec-Decani road as well as the Prilep-Junik road and hold a communication line by establishing checkpoints again in villages of Gornji Streoci and Donji Streoci. Now, who was holding the roads mentioned that you needed to liberate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Albanian terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these -- and these -- and these Albanian terrorists, how were they controlling the road? Were they shooting at people? Did they have checkpoints or roadblocks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both. They cut off road communication. They searched people and vehicles. They opened fire at people and vehicles. Looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, how long these Albanian terrorists had controlled that area of Kosovo and Metohija, that roadway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what month you were deployed in Gornja Streoci and Donji Streoci for the above mentioned tasks? Was it the possible that this was at the end of the month of May in 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall if during that time one could not travel from the city where you started out in Serbia, which I won't mention so as not to bring your identity into question, am I correct that you could not travel from that city into Kosovo and then go from Pec to Gornji and Donji Streoci directly but rather you had to travel over Montenegro to get to your location precisely because the Albanian terrorists, the UCK/KLA had already blocked and disrupted the main roads from Pristina to Pec and Mitrovica to Pec during that time period of approximately May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while your unit held the road between Gornji and Donji Streoci, did the KLA in fact engage in combat activities against your unit or any other unit engaged in holding that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there a similar checkpoint on the road in the village of Ljubenic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now, in the course of this deployment that we are talking about in Gornji and Donji Streoci, do you know how many killed or wounded policemen from your entire PJP detachment or other units that manned those checkpoints, do you know how many killed or wounded policemen there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know there were casualties, but I don't know the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my colleague, Mr. Ackerman, had already asked you about the deployment to try and retake Jablanica. I would just like to ask you with respect to that deployment, do you know -- did you -- did your unit or the other units involved suffer any casualties as a result of the actions -- the combat between yourselves and the armed terrorists in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we are talking about Jablanica, there were no casualties on our part there, but the exchange of fire was significant as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, in your statement, after discussing these deployments, you talk about, on page 5 of your statement, what you call your "last infamous" field deployment as being the one to blockade and mop up Junik and do the same with the mountain region by Junik. Now, am I correct that the use of this term "infamous" by you in your statement relates to the fact that a PJP position was subjected to friendly fire from other forces, namely the Yugoslav army, whereby several policemen, including a field commander, were killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were reading the transcript, I did mention that that was not the appropriate word. It doesn't convey the meaning of what I had intended to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And for each of your deployments in Kosovo, is it correct that your orders would be received from the various -- from within -- from the various PJP commanders, the individuals we discussed previously in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what it means, actually, is that we received orders from the commander of our company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct -- is it correct that those orders that you received from your superior officers, your commanders during your deployments in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999, am I correct that your tasks were at all times to prevent terrorist attacks by the KLA against civilians as well as against the MUP and the army? That is to say you were protecting everyone in Kosovo from the terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that your unit never received any orders from your police superiors to commit crimes against the civilians of Kosovo and Metohija, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact, am I correct that you were ordered by your superiors to safeguard civilian lives at all times during the carrying out of your tasks? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, specifically, when working and manning the checkpoints that we discussed previously, and in taking -- and in undertaking the other operations that you took part in, am I correct that you and your unit never had any orders from superiors -- your superiors, superior police officers, to engage in taking away identity documents from civilians and destroying them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And looking at the transcript it looks like I need to re-ask the question and -- at page 44 on line 7 because I asked a poor question that the yes answer could be read both ways for. Sir, did your unit ever receive any orders from your police superiors to commit crimes against civilians in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that clears things up. Now, am I correct that there were never any orders while manning the checkpoints or otherwise for you and the other policemen that were with you to take money, jewellery, or vehicles from these civilians? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I again asked a bad question. Were you ever given any orders by your police superiors while manning the checkpoints to take money, jewellery, or vehicles from Kosovo Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We did not receive such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you had previously testified about the reserve -- reservists in Kosovo and Metohija who were assigned by the military department to be in the police force. Is it a fact that due to the threat of the KLA and the threat of NATO military attack against Kosovo and Metohija that there was a general mobilisation covering the territory of the province of Kosovo and Metohija at that time in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as part of such a general mobilisation, wouldn't it be a fact that all reservists, whether army or -- whether assigned as army or police reservists, would therefore have to maintain arms with them as opposed to having the arms maintained in depots as was the case in Serbia proper at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They had to keep their weapons with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one thing. Was the general mobilisation actually confined to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I believe that in your direct examination you had said that you thought all the reservists were assigned to the local police. Am I correct that as a matter of fact you saw the persons, particularly in Velika and Mala Krusa, wearing all types of uniforms, not just police uniforms, as you stated in page 20, paragraph seven of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as far as reservists are concerned, am I correct that uniforms are issued to them, and they have those uniforms at all times, even when they are not called up by the military district and assigned to a particular role as part of a mobilisation? That is to say that persons in the reserve maintain their uniforms at their home even at times when they are not part of the active deployment of either the police or the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it from your earlier answers that you did not regard any of the persons wearing these miscellaneous uniforms as being paramilitaries. You regarded them all as part of regular forces or reservists.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as a follow-up to that: When you saw persons wearing these various uniforms, since you were not from the region and did not know anyone personally, you just assumed that these were members of the various legitimate local forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I would like to be clear about that. You're now saying something different. You're saying you just assumed that these people were members of legitimate local forces. Did you have any reason to doubt that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The local SUP, that is the local policemen who participated with us in our operation, were drawn in with exact positions on our maps that we received, so that I can't say that I doubted, because I knew that they were policemen from SUP Prizren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are these the people you're referring to as wearing a variety of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were people who passed by in military uniforms, but to our right was the army of Yugoslavia with their troops, so that they belonged to the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may assist. On page 20, he doesn't really say that the reservists were wearing a variety of uniforms. He specifies, rather, which kind of uniforms the MUP reservists wore and which the VJ reservists wore as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. You're referring to page 20 of the statement, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I thought that's what my learned colleague referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. He has already had an answer from the witness that people in Velika Krusa and Mala Krusa were wearing all sorts of uniforms, and it's on that that he's followed through and on that that I've asked a few questions. If you need to, you can deal with it in re-examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The three individuals, I believe you had said they were masked individuals in the police uniforms who you saw robbing various civilians on the roadway and whom your -- whom your commander confronted and tried to stop. Am I correct that those individuals drove away in a vehicle that was not a regular police vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I also correct that these persons, again these masked persons in police uniforms, they were not operating a checkpoint, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the position of the local police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I have a question here. Now, you had a mandate to arrest people who indulged in such an activity. Why didn't you arrest them when they were not the regular persons? They were driving a vehicle which didn't belong to the police. Why didn't you arrest them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they trained their guns at us, and we trained our guns at them, and there would have been casualties if we had done that. However, we did inform SUP Prizren, and sometimes it's not good to run such risks, because on the other hand we were facing a complete blockade, and we were subjected to terrorist action, and we could not afford to enter into conflict with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact there were civilians around you who would have been caught in the crossfire if there had been shooting. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did these three persons, these masked persons in police uniforms, did they then run away or escape? Is that the manner in which they got into the vehicle or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Or -- okay. Now, if I can direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All -- all the time we had our guns trained at one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can draw your attention now to your deployment, to the time of your deployment in Mala Krusa again, and specifically to the instructions given by your overall commander. Did you personally eyewitness the orders given by the commander, or were they conveyed to you by your ceta, commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of our company conveyed that to us, told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that the orders as conveyed to you were that you were instructed by your superior officers in the police to offer protection to any civilian villagers that chose to leave the village, as well as to offer protection to civilians who chose to stay in the villages? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that I received such an order, but generally speaking, that is our duty, our regular duty, and I don't see why that would have to be told expressly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In fact, that was understood and the regular duty of the police in any operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is a duty that arises under the law of the Republic of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so am I correct that such a duty to afford protection to civilians, this would have been offered by your unit and the other police equally to both Albanian and Serb villagers? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I really understood the interpretation. Could the interpreters repeat, please. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify by that, I mean there -- there was no distinction between how the Serb civilians or how the ethnic Albanian civilians or even how any ethnicity of civilians was -- was to be treated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while the operation was under way in the areas of Velika Krusa and Mala Krusa, am I correct that the civilians that did leave those villages were directed towards safety? That is to say they were directed towards an area outside the zone of operations for their safety?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was that so these civilians would not get caught in the crossfire between the KLA forces and the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you have described the operation in Mala Krusa as a "mop-up" operation. Based upon your knowledge of the activities of the police forces of the Republic of Serbia, am I correct in concluding that such operations are aimed at mopping up or clearing an area of terrorists and are not, in fact, directed against the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it also true, drawing upon your experience in other parts of Serbia, is it also true that a mop-up operation would also be carried out in other cities such as Belgrade or Novi Sad in order to remove any organised concentration of criminals from a given area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Has he the capacity to answer this question being a person at the lower echelons, as you yourself --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: -- put it to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he indicated he had been deployed as part of a PJP unit to other cities. So I asked him to draw upon that experience if in fact those operations were carried out in other cities aimed at criminals. I can ask the gentleman to explain if in fact that -- I can ask him if in fact he participated in such operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please do that, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in any operations outside of the republic of -- pardon, the province of Kosovo and Metohija that were termed mop-up operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the environs of Subotica when we had a serial killer, we did the same clearing of terrain or combing of terrain looking for that killer. In this case it was an individual, but that was the same kind of operation, and the whole PJP was engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now, were you familiar or -- were you familiar with a tactic of the armed terrorists in Kosovo, the KLA, removing their uniforms and discarding their weapons and dressing in civilian clothes to try and escape detection and get through Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they did that all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that in this operation, the operation at Velika Krusa, Mala Krusa, the local Prizren police were therefore endowed with the duty to seek out and identify potential KLA amongst any of the civilians based first on the information of their local RDB security organs and by performing a triage to filter such people out from amongst the legitimate civilians so they could be detained, arrested, and subjected to the appropriate judicial proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the source of your knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our order that we received when performing operations. We received a map where it was indicated where the checkpoint of the local police was and where the possible captives should be directed. And when refugee convoys started moving, they told us to send them towards the local SUP which would check whether there were any terrorists amongst them, because they knew almost all the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- now, apart -- excuse me. Apart from the incident with the three masked men who were trying to rob the civilians that your unit stopped and the incident with the -- with the three men wearing police uniforms whom you handed over the persons wearing the KLA uniforms, am I correct that you did not witness any other criminal acts being undertaken by anyone wearing a police uniform as part of this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. I did not observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And dealing with these two incidents, am I correct that at all times you saw no more than three total individuals wearing police uniforms engaged in such acts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can have Exhibit P1326 brought up. This should be one of the items that the witness looked at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We certainly had -- oh, yes, we did have 1326.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you previously talked about the picture which is labelled number 4 in this photograph, and I wanted to ask you about the brown belt that is being worn by this individual in this picture. Is that brown belt a part of the regular uniform of the Serbian police when it is operating on the terrain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is that the reason why you identified this photograph yesterday as probably being a police reservist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the fact that the man is not shaven.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does the Serbian MUP have such brown belts in the inventory of its official equipment, it's official uniforms, brown leather?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, based upon your knowledge and experience, did you have any knowledge of incidents or reports of persons who misused uniforms, that is to say the illegitimate use of police and other uniforms by criminals on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We heard such cases. In fact, I heard about such cases wherein Albanians wore our uniforms trying to attract the attention of our forces, and sometimes that resulted in exchanges of fire, and I believe in one case in the death of one policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as far as the -- as far as your other deployments, that is to say the deployments preceding your deployment to Mala Krusa and your deployments after Mala Krusa, am I correct that during none of these deployments did you witness any criminal acts carried out against Kosovo Albanian civilians by your fellow policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not witness that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to -- one moment. I need to find a reference here.
